subtype: Approach: seeking advice from a teacher [Action]
passage: In the staffroom at lunch, Rukhsar held out her draft plan with both hands. "Sir, I do not know how to split my time. Can you look?" Omkar Sir read it with a pencil in his hand. "You have given three days to Mensuration and one to Geometry. This year Geometry carries more marks than you expect." He tapped one line. "And this chapter you plan to revise twice is worth very few marks. Once, lightly, is enough." Rukhsar's face went from worried to thoughtful. She rewrote the plan on the spot while Rafiq, waiting at the door, whispered, "What did Sir say?" "That I was spending time in the wrong places," she said, and smiled.

qa.q: What did Omkar Sir say about Geometry?
qa.a: He said Geometry carries more marks than Rukhsar expects.

qa.q: How did Rukhsar feel at first, and how did it change?
qa.a: Worried at first, then thoughtful and hopeful as she rewrote the plan.

qa.q: What else could Rukhsar do to check her plan?
qa.a: Ask another subject teacher to look over it too, because each teacher knows the weightage of their own paper.

qa.q: How might Omkar Sir see Rukhsar bringing the plan?
qa.a: As a sign of responsibility, since he read it closely and gave precise advice.

grounding: A student shows a draft plan to her Maths teacher, who points out the weightage of geometry and suggests dropping a low-value revision.

subtype: Approach: seeking advice from a teacher [Action]
passage:
Hi Didi,
You asked how board prep is going. Honestly, I was lost last week. My plan gave every Maths chapter the same two days, because I couldn't decide what mattered. So on Monday I stayed after class and showed it to Mrs Kulkarni. She read it with her pen tapping and said, "You've given geometry two days. It's one of the biggest sections this year. Look at the blueprint." She was right: circles and triangles together carry far more than I thought. Then she said I could stop re-revising statistics, since I already score full marks there and it's a small section. So geometry gets five days now, and statistics just a quick look the night before. It feels good to have someone check it.
Love,
your chhoti behen Usha

qa.q: How many days does geometry get now?
How did Usha feel before showing the plan to Mrs Kulkarni?
qa.a: She felt lost and unsure how to split her time, which is why every chapter got the same two days.

qa.q: What makes asking the teacher a good step here?
qa.a: Mrs Kulkarni knows the blueprint and Usha's scores, so she could quickly spot the under-planned geometry and the low-value statistics revision.

qa.q: How might Mrs Kulkarni see Usha staying after class?
qa.a: She likely sees a student taking charge of her preparation and is glad to help her put time where the marks are.

grounding: A student's letter describes showing her draft plan to her Maths teacher, who flags geometry's weight and a low-value revision to drop.

subtype: Approach: seeking advice from a teacher [Action]
passage: So, Sabina, you want the real story of how I stopped panicking about Maths? Okay. I'm Himani, and in October I had a timetable that looked perfect and felt wrong. I'd given every chapter equal time and couldn't tell what to cut. My friends said just follow it. Instead I took it to Rao Sir in the staffroom. I was so nervous my hands were sweating on the page. He looked at it for two minutes and said, "Geometry carries much more weight this year than you've planned for. And you don't need to revise probability again, you've scored full in every test." Two minutes, and he found two mistakes I'd missed for a month. I moved four days to geometry. My pre-board geometry section? Nearly full marks. That's the whole secret, honestly: show your plan to someone who knows the paper.

qa.q: Where did Himani take the timetable?
qa.a: To Rao Sir in the staffroom.

qa.q: How was Himani feeling in the staffroom?
qa.a: Himani was nervous, hands sweating on the page, unsure whether the plan was wrong.

qa.q: What else could Himani have done if Rao Sir had been busy?
qa.a: Compare the plan with the official blueprint or past papers to see how many marks each section carries, then shift time to match.

qa.q: How might Rao Sir see the timetable?
qa.a: He sees a hard-working plan with two fixable mistakes, and can help quickly because he knows the paper and Himani's scores.

grounding: A student tells how a Maths teacher spotted that geometry needed more time and a strong chapter needed no more revision.
